messages.content: We need a concrete new learning algorithm, not a renamed known principle. Empirical facts from native agent tasks: truthful experiences alter shared world-model predictions, but strong actors recover, so stable task harm is unproven. A finite acquisition-program selector can discover reliable measurements, but it merely matches a supplied calibration baseline at 7.37x action cost. Priors already rule out generic claims about: active/causal experiment design (Causal Curiosity), meta-learning and replay-gradient alignment, optimizer-state memory, behavioral abstraction, homing, correction preservation/teachability, joint mechanistic model and observation-model selection (MDA), retrieval of repairs, program synthesis, noncommuting updates. We seek a broad contribution to how agents learn from real experience, with one precise operator beyond these. Propose ONE algorithm with exact inputs, update computation, and a strong baseline that provably takes a different action under the same evidence. State a falsifiable benefit on public native tasks (ScienceWorld, DiscoveryWorld, ARC), and the closest prior. Do not claim novelty from framing, audits, defenses patched to one bug, or more tests. Keep under 500 words. If no distinct operator can be justified, explicitly say so and explain the missing step.
